newsitem.title: GERMANY: ETA suspect turns herself in to German police.
newsitem.headline: ETA suspect turns herself in to German police.

text.p: A German woman accused by Spain of aiding the violent Basque separatist group ETA turned herself in to German police and is in investigative custody, prosecutors in the city of Wiesbaden said on Wednesday.
A spokesman for prosecutors Wolfgang Greth named the woman as Heike Schubbert and said she had handed herself over to police in the central German city accompanied by her lawyer on Tuesday.
Schubbert, a 33-year-old student from Wiesbaden, is the daughter of a mid-level Bundesbank (German central bank) official.

Spanish police say she signed the rental contract for a safe house in Madrid where suspected ETA guerrillas stored weapons and explosives and suspect she was one of four people who fled last April shortly before an accidental explosion.
ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) has killed about 800 people in a campaign of violence for an independent Basque state that has lasted almost 29 years.

German prosecutors are also investigating another German, Fritz Siemund, who is suspected of belonging to an ETA cell operating in the Spanish capital and believed to be behind several attacks in Madrid.
He was arrested in the German town of Wiesbaden in April at the request of Spanish police. Schubbert is his suspected accomplice, prosecutors said.
